RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Raising the panel's gender composition would be counterproductive and lacks merit. Because both you and the successful candidate are women, claiming sex discrimination is legally and factually unfounded. An all-women panel selecting one female candidate over another offers no evidence of sex-based bias.

Executive hiring for director-level roles often hinges on strategic communication, political acumen, and stakeholder engagement—strengths highlighted in the announcement—rather than purely technical planning credentials or seniority. Furthermore, a two-week turnaround for municipal HR feedback is typical.

Mentioning the panel's gender will harm your professional reputation. Instead, send a polite follow-up inquiry focusing exclusively on constructive feedback regarding interview performance and executive competencies.
